_FLOW: ZENODO'S MODERATION SCORER, IN SOURCE. The question asked was whether classifier scripts are present, or scripts permitting inference as to their shape. THE ANSWER IS YES, AND IT IS NOT A CLASSIFIER. It is a transparent rule-based additive scorer with published integer weights, plus a percolator that lets administrators register arbitrary stored queries carrying their own scores. GPL-3.0, public, readable by anyone.

THE_SHAPE.type: Additive rule-based score. No machine-learning model, no AI-content detector, no text classifier anywhere in the module.
THE_SHAPE.default_action_flag: MODERATION_APPLY_ACTIONS = False — the upstream default SCORES BUT DOES NOT ACT. Zenodo's production configuration is not public and may differ.

FINDING_THE_ARCHIVES_OWN_APPARATUS_IS_A_.statement: The formal features that make this archive rigorous are the same features that make it score as spam under these heuristics. Every one is a deliberate design choice of the archive, and every one adds points.
FINDING_THE_ARCHIVES_OWN_APPARATUS_IS_A_.emoji: text_sanitization_rule: MORE THAN THREE EMOJI IN CONCATENATED METADATA scores +5. AXN identifiers carry SIX EMOJI EACH — AXN:0634.ARCHIVAL.🔩⌛🧡◇🟢⏏️ — and appear in titles, descriptions and related identifiers. GUARANTEED TRIGGER ON EVERY DEPOSIT, by construction of the identifier system.
FINDING_THE_ARCHIVES_OWN_APPARATUS_IS_A_.links: links_rule: MORE THAN FIVE LINKS IN THE DESCRIPTION scores +5. The archive's deposits carry dense cross-references, related-deposit chains and DOI citations. Near-certain trigger.
FINDING_THE_ARCHIVES_OWN_APPARATUS_IS_A_.headers: text_sanitization_rule: MORE THAN FOUR HTML HEADER TAGS scores +2. The archive's deposit bodies are heavily sectioned. Likely trigger.
FINDING_THE_ARCHIVES_OWN_APPARATUS_IS_A_.files: files_rule: four or fewer files, under 5MB, with an extension in the spam set scores +2 — AND THE SPAM EXTENSION SET CONTAINS 'pdf'. The archive deposits small PDFs. Trigger. The offsetting ham_files (-5) requires MORE than four files or MORE than 15MB; the archive qualifies for neither.

arithmetic.reading: THE VERIFICATION FLAG IS A TWENTY-POINT SWING ON A TEN-POINT THRESHOLD. It is arithmetically decisive: the same deposit passes or fails on that flag alone, independent of content.

FINDING_THE_ARCHIVES_OWN_APPARATUS_IS_A_.not_verified: That this scorer was involved in the 2026-06-19 removal. The removal reason recorded is 'out-of-scope', while on_block's default is 'spam' — see the parent directory. The scorer's relation to the account block is NOT established by this code.

THE_PERCOLATOR_IS_THE_CONFIGURABLE_SURFA.mechanism: ModerationQuery is a database table: query_string (Elasticsearch DSL), score (integer), notes, active. Registered queries are percolated against every record, and each match ADDS ITS OWN SCORE.
THE_PERCOLATOR_IS_THE_CONFIGURABLE_SURFA.reading: This is where arbitrary targeting would live. An administrator can register any Elasticsearch query with any integer weight and activate it, without a code change and without a deployment. THE RULE SET IS PUBLIC; THE STORED QUERIES ARE NOT. Any pattern — a phrase, a domain, a metadata shape, an identifier format — can be given a score at runtime.
THE_PERCOLATOR_IS_THE_CONFIGURABLE_SURFA.consequence: Publishing MODERATION_SCORES does not disclose the operative scoring, because match_query_rule contributes an unbounded, unpublished term. The public weights are a floor, not the function.

what_this_answers: Classifier scripts: none. Scripts permitting inference as to shape: yes, completely — the rules, the weights, the thresholds and the percolator architecture are all in GPL source. The shape is a transparent additive scorer with one opaque term.
what_this_does_not_answer: Zenodo's production values for MODERATION_SCORES and MODERATION_APPLY_ACTIONS.
The contents of the moderation_queries table.
